newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR says unlikely to fully frank divs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR says unlikely to fully frank divs.

text.p: Building materials, aluminiun and sugar producer CSR Ltd said on Monday it was extraordinarily unlikely that it would be able to fully frank its dividends over the next three to four years because a large portion of its earnings will come from overseas units.
CSR chairman Alan Coates said this meant CSR would struggle to frank its dividends by more than 50 percent over this period.
"It would be fair to say for the foreseeable future, perhaps the next three to four years, it's extraordinarily unlikely that we'd be able to fully frank our dividends," Coates told the meeting.
"In fact, we'll be struggling to maintain an appropriate level of franking, say of 50 percent," he said.
Coates said the group aimed to increase profits over the coming years from its Australian operations, but this would be not nearly enough to restore full franking.
He said the government's changes announced in this year's budget to tax rules over the trading of franking credits meant CSR would also be unlikely to acquire franking credits.
"You'll have to accept that for the next few years, franking credits are not going to get up anywhere near 100 percent," he said.

Australia's tax system treats dividends from those companies earning most of their profits in Australia as already taxed. They are then deemed to be franked and are treated as tax-free income in personal tax returns.
CSR posted full-year dividends for the year to March 31, 1997, of 21 cents, down from 29 cents in the previous year. The 1996-97 dividend was 50-percent franked.
